You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
" *

Adds all the elements of the given arrays into a new array.

*

The new array contains all of the element of array1 followed * by all of the elements array2. When an array is returned, it is always * a new array.

* * 
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, null)     = null
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(array1, null)   = cloned copy of array1
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, array2)   = cloned copy of array2
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([], [])         = []
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([null], [null]) = [null, null]
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(["a", "b", "c"], ["1", "2", "3"]) = ["a", "b", "c", "1", "2", "3"]
     *
* * @param array1 the first array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @param array2 the second array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @return The new array, null if both arrays are null. * The type of the new array is the type of the first array, * unless the first array is null, in which case the type is the same as the second array. * @since 2.1 "

Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The failing test is exercising the method `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)` with two arrays of different but related types: an `Integer[]` and a `Long[]`, both subclasses of `Number`. According to the method implementation, it first checks if either array is null and returns a clone of the other if so. Otherwise, it extracts the component type of the first array (`array1.getClass().getComponentType()`) and creates a new array of that type with combined length. It then copies the content of `array1` at the start, and copies the contents of `array2` into this new array after `array1`.

The problem arises at the copy of `array2` into the new array (at line 2962). Since the new array's type is strictly the type of the first array (in this case `Integer`), trying to copy `Long` elements into it via `System.arraycopy` raises an `ArrayStoreException` from the JVM, because `Long` cannot be stored in an `Integer` array. The symptom in the exception message is an `ArrayStoreException`. The test expects an `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown instead, indicating that the current `addAll` method does not properly detect or handle mixed array types that are not directly compatible to avoid the JVM error.

The javadoc and method behavior show that the type of the new array is chosen solely based on the first array's component type and does not check compatibility of the second array's elements beforehand. This leads to a confusing low-level runtime error instead of a clear and meaningful validation error.

The current bug report also indicates this by stating the stack trace is not obvious and the user expects a clearer exception than `ArrayStoreException`. The test failure confirms that the method does not handle this mixed-type array scenario safely.

Recent bug reports unrelated and do not pertain to array handling or type safety in `addAll`.

In conclusion, the root cause is that `ArrayUtils.addAll` does not validate if the second array's contents can be safely stored in an array of the first array's component type, leading to a runtime `ArrayStoreException`. The desired behavior would be to detect this incompatibility and throw an `IllegalArgumentException` upfront instead.

The faulty behavior is specifically at the array creation and copy lines:
- The method does not check that elements of array2 can be assigned to `type1`
- The method tries to store them blindly, leading to JVM `ArrayStoreException` when incompatible

A fix should add a validation step before array creation or copying to detect incompatible element types and throw an appropriate exception.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
